desc:
Count the non-empty contiguous subarrays of nums whose first element and last element are both equal to the maximum of the subarray. A subarray with a single element always qualifies. Subarrays at different positions count separately even if they hold the same values.

Example: for [1, 4, 3, 3, 2] the answer is 6: the five single elements and [3, 3]. For [3, 3, 3] the answer is 6 as well: three single elements, two subarrays [3, 3] and one [3, 3, 3].
hints: A qualifying subarray ends at some index r, and its start l ≤ r must hold the same value as nums[r] with nothing larger in between. Count the valid starts for each end r.

For a fixed end r the valid starts are the earlier indices l with nums[l] == nums[r] such that every element between them is at most nums[r], plus r itself. A larger element between two equal values cuts them off from each other.

Keep a stack of [value, count] pairs with strictly decreasing values from bottom to top. For a new value x, pop all pairs with a value smaller than x; if the top now has value x increase its count, otherwise push [x, 1]. The top count is the number of valid starts for this end, so add it to the answer.
editorial: Count the subarrays by their last index r. The first element l must satisfy nums[l] == nums[r] and no element in between may exceed that value, otherwise the maximum would differ from the ends. So for each r we need the number of indices l ≤ r that are still 'visible' to r with the same value, counting r itself.

A monotonic stack of [value, count] pairs maintains exactly that. When a larger value arrives, every smaller value on the stack is blocked for all later ends, so it is popped. If the new top equals the new value, those earlier copies are still reachable and the new copy joins the group (count + 1); otherwise a new group with count 1 is started. The group count at the top is the number of valid starts for the current end. Each element is pushed and popped at most once, so the time is O(n); space is O(n). The answer is at most n(n+1)/2, which fits into 32 bits for n ≤ 50,000.
